text:
maria: nightly-eval-bot alerted a big jump in failures after the promptset v11 change — +12% neg-case on the summarization pset. attaching report: https://ci.redwood/models/pset11/regression. failing examples look like label flips and weird truncation.
nightly-eval-bot: [auto] pset: pset-summarize-v11, model: redwood-v2-q, metric: neg_case_rate, baseline: 0.032 -> 0.144 (12pp), samples_failed: 48/332. diffs attached.
zach: ouch. did pset11 change expected wording or normalization rules?
maria: pset11 mostly updated a bunch of reference outputs (removed extraneous punctuation and standardized dates). no prompt wording changes. also note model used is the quantized candidate redwood-v2-q (brought up yesterday).
lee: can you paste a minimal failing example inline? helps narrow whether it's matching logic or generation shift.
maria: sure — here's one failing item (old golden vs new model output):
```
PROMPT: "Summarize: The meeting on 2024-11-01 concluded with action items."
GOLDEN: "Meeting concluded with action items on 2024-11-01."
MODEL(v1): "Meeting concluded with action items on 2024-11-01."
MODEL(v2-q): "Meeting concluded with action items"
// note: v2-q dropped the date token at the end
```
eva: that looks like a truncation / tokenization mismatch — dropped trailing token (date). could be quantization or tokenizer change. also pset cleanup removed punctuation so boundary tokens changed.
zach: also check eval runner: we recently flipped normalize_whitespace = true to reduce spam diffs. could that affect tokenization or the post-compare pipeline?
maria: i ran a quick local reproduce: with normalize_whitespace=false the v2-q delta shrinks to +1.2%. with it on, plus pset11 refs, it's the +12%.
lee: so two axes: pset ref changes (matching stricter/simpler strings) and eval postprocessing. which commit flipped normalize_whitespace?
maria: eval-config history shows: 2024-11-15 jd toggled normalize_whitespace: false -> true in eval-runner config. pset11 merge was 2024-11-18. redwood-v2-q deployment yesterday.
zach: hypothesis: pset rebaseline removed punctuation so compare now relies more on exact token boundaries; normalize_whitespace collapse might be triggering different token offsets for quantized tokenizer, exposing truncation.
eva: recommendation: 1) roll-back normalize_whitespace in nightly-dev branch and re-run; 2) run tokenizer token-sequence diff between model tokenizers; 3) add a tolerant compare mode for dates/ISO strings or postnormalize dates to a stable canonical form.
maria: I'll do 1 & 2 now. token-diff command I ran: `python -m evals.tools.token_diff --model redwood-v2 --model redwood-v2-q --sample "Meeting concluded with action items on 2024-11-01."` result: token sequences differ at the last 2 tokens for v2-q (it merges date into one token vs v2 separate tokens).
zach: that would explain dropped date after quantized decode, if decoder EOS handling differs. also check beam/greedy differences in runtime.
jd: saw the tag — my normalize change was to reduce noise from incidental whitespace. happy to revert on nightly branch while you triage.
maria: thanks @jd. I'll open a quick revert PR for eval-config and kick another nightly run against pset11 + redwood-v2-q. i'll also run the tokenizer diff across a broader sample to see how widespread these merges are. will report back in this thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jd: thanks, keep me posted. if we confirm it's quantization-induced token merges, we should add a targeted unit test for date-like tokens in the quantization pipeline.
maria: agreed — adding to checklist. followups: (1) revert normalize -> rerun tonight (2) run token-diff for 100 random pset items (3) if regression persists, consider rolling pset11 rebaseline or add a tolerant matcher for date-like entities.
lee: fine plan. ping if you need help with the nightly runner or infra.
maria: will do. updating the CI ticket: https://ci.redwood/issue/INF-842.
nightly-eval-bot: [auto] rerun scheduled on branch: nightly-dev once PR #482 is merged.
